title: 4 of Google’s Top AI Brains Are Leaving—and Launching Their Own AI Startup
gist: After nearly 27 years at Google, Jeff Dean (Google Brain cofounder, DeepMind/Research chief scientist, Gemini technical colead) is leaving with longtime collaborator Sanjay Ghemawat and fellow AI leaders Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le to found Discovery Loop, a startup betting on fully automated experiment loops (propose-implement-evaluate-iterate) to accelerate scientific and engineering discovery across ML, chip design, biology and materials; Google is taking a stake and providing a year of compute, and VCs Khosla Ventures and Radical Ventures backed the round sight-unseen on team reputation alone.

themes.theme: The exodus and what it costs Google

insights.claim: Jeff Dean — cofounder of Google Brain, chief scientist of Google DeepMind and Google Research, and technical colead on Gemini — is leaving Google after almost 27 years, along with longtime collaborator Sanjay Ghemawat, to found Discovery Loop; Google will take a stake in the new company.
insights.speaker: Steven Levy
insights.so_what: The departure of Google's most technically foundational engineer after 27 years, even with Google retaining an equity stake, is a material loss of institutional AI leadership at a company competing head-to-head with OpenAI and Anthropic on frontier models.
insights.locator: Today it's official: After almost 27 years, Dean is leaving Google

insights.claim: Oriol Vinyals, VP of research at DeepMind and a technical lead for Gemini, and Quoc Le, a cofounder of Google Brain and the key scientist behind Google's AutoML-Zero project, are also cofounding Discovery Loop alongside Dean and Ghemawat.
insights.speaker: Steven Levy
insights.so_what: All four cofounders held senior technical leadership roles directly tied to Gemini and Google's core ML research, meaning this is a coordinated departure of a critical mass of Gemini-adjacent talent, not a single-person exit.
insights.locator: Worse, the other cofounders are also supernovas

insights.claim: Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai tried over multiple meetings to convince the team to stay at Google, and ultimately Google gave the departing engineers its blessing along with an investment and an arrangement to provide compute power for Discovery Loop's first year.
insights.speaker: Steven Levy
insights.so_what: Google chose to retain a stake and compute partnership rather than lose the relationship entirely, suggesting a strategic calculation that partial ownership/access to Discovery Loop's output is more valuable than an adversarial split — a template other AI incumbents may use for staff spinouts.
insights.quote: Over 27 years, Jeff and Sanjay helped to drive some of the most significant technology transitions, from our early search infrastructure to the neural networks that helped create the modern AI era.
insights.locator: Negotiating the exit from Google was more painful

insights.claim: Because the founders have deliberately maintained stealth and have not yet hired a team or rented office space, the article notes this could mean even more departures from Google as the team builds out staff.
insights.speaker: Steven Levy
insights.so_what: Signals a likely second wave of Google AI talent attrition as Discovery Loop staffs up, a leading indicator investors and competing labs should watch for continued Google brain-drain risk.
insights.locator: they haven't yet begun to hire a team

insights.claim: Dean's core idea, which he described publicly at Y Combinator's Startup School before revealing it was his own startup, is an automated version of the scientific method: propose an experiment, implement what's needed to run it, evaluate the results, and iterate — with the belief that running thousands of these loops could unlock advances across science, biology, chip design, and AI model improvement itself.
insights.speaker: Jeff Dean (via Steven Levy)
insights.so_what: Frames Discovery Loop's core bet as automating the scientific method itself at scale — if successful, this could compress R&D cycle times across multiple deep-tech verticals (chips, drugs, materials) simultaneously, a much broader thesis than a single-domain AI product.
insights.locator: You propose an experiment, you implement what you need

insights.claim: Discovery Loop's roadmap is to be its own first customer: initial automated experiment loops will be directed at improving the company's own machine learning algorithms, and that improved software will then become the core of an AI system applied to subsequent domains including chip design, biology, drug discovery, and material design.
insights.speaker: Steven Levy
insights.so_what: A recursive self-improvement bootstrap strategy (use the tool to improve the tool, then generalize) is a distinctive go-to-market sequencing choice that, if it works, could compound capability faster than building separate domain-specific tools from scratch.
insights.locator: The quartet worked up a road map

insights.claim: Cofounder Quoc Le says he is excited about automating machine learning itself and speculates Discovery Loop might discover a different transformer architecture; cofounder Oriol Vinyals says a key focus will be how the models come up with genuinely new ideas to try, which he says is not something current AI systems are 'super strong at.'
insights.speaker: Quoc Le and Oriol Vinyals (via Steven Levy)
insights.so_what: A direct admission from two of the field's top researchers that current AI models are weak at generating genuinely novel research ideas — an honest capability gap assessment from insiders that tempers hype about near-term autonomous AI scientific discovery.
insights.quote: One of the things that we'll be obviously very focused on is how these models come up with new ideas to try. That's not something that currently they're super strong at.
insights.locator: One of the things that we'll be obviously very focused on

insights.claim: The founders envision that a few dedicated individuals using Discovery Loop could eventually out-invent the world's largest research organizations, positioning small teams as potential customers, while Discovery Loop itself may also build its own loops to seek and monetize breakthroughs directly.
insights.speaker: Steven Levy
insights.so_what: Implies a dual business model — selling the discovery-automation platform to small teams AND directly monetizing in-house breakthroughs — giving Discovery Loop two distinct potential revenue paths (B2B tooling and proprietary IP generation).
insights.locator: If it works out, they contend, it's possible

insights.claim: Venture capitalist Vinod Khosla says he backed the founders without needing to know the specifics of what they were building, based purely on the team's reputation, meeting them in his Sand Hill Road office on a Saturday specifically so no one would get advance notice of Google's coming loss; Khosla Ventures and Radical Ventures led the round, along with a handful of other firms, with the exact funding amount and valuation undisclosed.
insights.speaker: Vinod Khosla (via Steven Levy)
insights.so_what: A top-tier VC funding a startup purely on team pedigree, without a product or disclosed business plan beyond a slide deck, illustrates how extreme AI-talent scarcity has pushed venture capital into pattern-matching on reputation alone for pre-product deep-tech bets — an environment where founder brand can substitute entirely for traction.
insights.quote: With this team, I wouldn't need to know what they were doing before I backed them. It's the ultimate superstar team.

insights.claim: Khosla frames Discovery Loop's core innovation as a categorical shift: 'Humans have been using AI to do research, not using AI to be a researcher... The fundamental thing [in Discovery Loop] is that AI is the researcher.'
insights.speaker: Vinod Khosla (via Steven Levy)
insights.so_what: A crisp framework distinguishing 'AI as research tool' from 'AI as the researcher itself' — useful for evaluating whether other AI-for-science startups are making an incremental tooling play or a more ambitious, higher-risk full-automation bet like Discovery Loop.
insights.quote: Humans have been using AI to do research, not using AI to be a researcher. The fundamental thing [in Discovery Loop] is that AI is the researcher.
insights.locator: Humans have been using AI to do research

insights.claim: The article notes that some companies are currently paying tens or even hundreds of millions of dollars to acquire a single AI superstar researcher, contextualizing the scale of value the market currently places on this caliber of talent as Discovery Loop's four cofounders left together.
insights.speaker: Steven Levy
insights.so_what: Provides a market-rate anchor (tens to hundreds of millions per individual AI star hire) against which to judge the implied value of Discovery Loop's four-person founding team, suggesting the round likely carries an unusually high implied valuation relative to any disclosed product.
insights.locator: consider that some companies are paying tens or even hundreds of millions
